posts.title: What a 10-hour day really looks like
posts.excerpt: Three fixed points, a morning of rain and a plan that was allowed to change: one full day with the Brandt family.
posts.content:
A ten-hour day with Kuruma Tabi starts at 08:30 in your hotel lobby and ends at 18:00 at the same door. In between there are only three fixed points: a ridge viewpoint, a harbour lunch and a walk by the lake. Everything else is left loose on purpose.

The Brandt family from Hamburg arrived for a full day planned around the Alder Hills. When morning rain moved across the ridge, their driver-guide did not cancel the viewpoint; he moved it. They took the sheltered cedar path first, had lunch at the harbour while the clouds lifted, and reached the ridge in the last light of the afternoon.

That is the whole idea of one vehicle for one family. A plan is a draft Mika sends within twenty-four hours of your request, and the day itself is allowed to change. The fare covers the driver-guide, fuel, tolls and parking, so a longer lunch or an extra stop costs you nothing but time.
